title: Classic Pepper Steak with Green Peppers and Tomatoes
instructions: Cut beef into strips measuring 1/4-inch by 2 inches. (This will be easier to do if meat is partially frozen.) Heat oil in a saute pan over medium-high heat. Add meat and cook until meat is browned, about 5 minutes per side.
Add water, onion, garlic, ginger, and salt. Bring to a boil. Reduce heat, cover, and simmer until beef is tender, about 20 minutes. Add half of the peppers to the pan.

In a small bowl, combine cornstarch, sugar, and soy sauce. Stir into beef mixture. Raise heat and stir constantly as mixture thickens and comes to a boil. Lower heat and add tomatoes and remaining peppers. Cover and cook for an additional 3 minutes. Serve over hot rice.

tips.title: Health Note: green vs. colored peppers
tips.text: All peppers are green when they begin to grow. As they ripen, their sugar content increases and they turn colors - that's why brightly colored peppers are sweeter than green ones, which are picked earlier and have a sharp, bitter taste. It's also why green peppers are less expensive than red: they don't take as long to grow.

notes: Meat recipe, kosher as written. Source: photo of a cookbook page (p. 141, MEAT & POULTRY section).
